title: Classifying special quadrilaterals by their properties
summary: Classify quadrilaterals from sides, angles, diagonals and symmetry.
objectives: Classify special quadrilaterals from their sides, angles and parallel sides.
Use diagonal and symmetry properties to distinguish related quadrilaterals.
Explain the hierarchy linking squares, rectangles, rhombi and parallelograms.

blocks.text: A square is both a rectangle and a rhombus. Rectangles and rhombi are parallelograms. A kite has two pairs of adjacent equal sides. A trapezium has exactly one pair of parallel sides (in American English it is called a trapezoid).

Quadrilaterals form a hierarchy: every square is also a rectangle, a rhombus and a parallelogram, and every rectangle and every rhombus is a parallelogram. The diagram shows a kite, which is not in this family: its single and double tick marks show two pairs of adjacent equal sides. In a parallelogram the equal sides are opposite each other instead, and in a rhombus all four sides are equal.

Classify a figure by the most specific set of guaranteed properties. Sides and angles often narrow the class first; diagonals then distinguish related shapes. Rectangle diagonals are equal and bisect each other. Rhombus diagonals are perpendicular and bisect each other. Square diagonals have both sets of properties.

sections.title: Worked example: classify from the diagonals

prompt.text: A parallelogram has equal diagonals that are not perpendicular. Classify it as specifically as possible.

content.text: The diagonals of every parallelogram bisect each other. A parallelogram whose diagonals are also equal is a rectangle.
The diagonals are not perpendicular, so it is not a rhombus, and therefore not a square.

sections.verification_note: A rectangle that is not a square fits every condition: its diagonals bisect each other and are equal, but they do not meet at 90°.

sections.title: Worked example: combine two properties

prompt.text: A parallelogram has perpendicular diagonals and one right angle. Classify it as specifically as possible.

content.text: One right angle in a parallelogram makes all four angles right angles, so it is a rectangle.
Perpendicular diagonals in a parallelogram make it a rhombus.
A quadrilateral that is both a rectangle and a rhombus is a square.

sections.verification_note: A square satisfies every stated property: opposite sides parallel, four right angles and perpendicular diagonals that bisect each other.

blocks.text: Do not stop at a broad name when a more specific one is guaranteed. Equal diagonals alone do not prove a square, and perpendicular diagonals alone do not prove a square. Combine all given properties before classifying.

prompt.text: A parallelogram has perpendicular diagonals but no right angle. Which shape must it be? Enter 1 for rectangle, 2 for rhombus, 3 for square or 4 for kite.

feedback.text: Perpendicular diagonals make a parallelogram a rhombus. With no right angle it cannot be a rectangle or a square, so the answer is 2 (rhombus).

blocks.text: Square = rectangle and rhombus; rectangles and rhombi are parallelograms. A kite has two pairs of adjacent equal sides, and a trapezium has exactly one pair of parallel sides.
Classify with every given property, using sides and angles first and diagonals second, and give the most specific name that is guaranteed.
